sub_answers.text: She frequently appeared as a romantic/leading heroine early in her career, notably as the heroine in Bedara Kannappa and Parasakthi [d72366297s0p0]. She repeatedly embodied maternal figures later in her career and acted as mother to major stars across languages [d72366297s0p0]. Tulasi became identified with screen-mother roles after marriage, with a turning-point mother role in the Kannada film Excuse Me and many subsequent mother parts in Telugu and Tamil films [d41179500s1p0]. Anjali Devi played a wide range of archetypes across myth, classical and traditional roles, including the role of Sita in the landmark 1963 film Lava Kusa [d15550665s2p0]. Sanjjana took on more daring and supporting/character roles in multiple languages, including a salsa-dancer role in the 2012 Malayalam film Casanova and attention-gaining supporting work in the Telugu film Bujjigadu (2008) and Kannada Ganda Hendathi (2006) [d19540993s2p0][d19540993s0p0].
